prompt: Where does the code of a Cypress test run?

choices.text: In a Node process that sends each step to the browser over HTTP
choices.why: That is Selenium's arrangement in lesson 8: the test outside, a driver carrying each command in.

choices.text: As a script in a page inside the browser
choices.why: Right. The runner is a page of Cypress's own, the spec runs in it, and the application sits in a frame beside it.

choices.text: In the Cypress server, which reads the page through its proxy
choices.why: The server stands in the network path, but the test's commands run in the browser, not beside it.

choices.text: In a second tab that watches the application's tab
choices.why: There is one tab: the runner and the application are frames of the same window.

prompt: A test needs to replace one of the shop's functions with a stub while the page runs. Why is that direct in Cypress?

choices.text: Its proxy rewrites the function inside `app.js` as the file is served
choices.why: The proxy sees requests, but a stub replaces a live function in the page; that needs the page's `window`, which the spec already shares.

choices.text: It copies the function across a socket and sends a new one back
choices.why: That is the outside model, and a function does not survive being copied as a message.

choices.text: The spec shares the browser with the page, so its `window` is in reach
choices.why: Right. `cy.window()` hands over the page's own object, and `cy.stub()` replaces a function on it.

choices.text: Electron allows it and other browsers refuse
choices.why: It works the same in Chrome and Firefox; what makes it possible is where the test runs, not which browser.

prompt: Match each piece to its job.

pairs.right: Loads the spec as a script on its page
Stands between the browser and the network
Carries a Selenium command into Chrome

prompt: `npm install` finished with no error, and `npx cypress --version` prints `Cypress binary version: not installed`. What happened?

choices.text: npm failed in silence and has to be run again with `--force`
choices.why: npm did its half; the binary is a separate download that came after it, and that is what is missing.

choices.text: The package is installed and its binary is not
choices.why: Right. The first line names the package's version; the second says the download never arrived.

choices.text: `package.json` pins a version that does not exist
choices.why: Then npm itself would have failed; it printed the package version, 16.1.1.

choices.text: A browser has to be installed before Cypress
choices.why: The binary brings its own browser, Electron; nothing has to come first.

prompt: You upgrade the `cypress` package to a newer version. `npx cypress verify` now says no version is installed, though you downloaded a binary last month. Why?

choices.text: Upgrading a package empties the caches in the home folder
choices.why: The old binary is still in the cache; it is simply in the old version's folder.

choices.text: The binary lived in `node_modules`, which npm replaced
choices.why: It lives outside the project, in a cache folder in your home directory.

choices.text: The cache keeps one folder per release, and the new release looks in its own
choices.why: Right. The path in the message ends in the version number; a new version means a new download.

choices.text: `verify` needs the network each time it runs
choices.why: It starts the local binary; the network is only needed to download one.

prompt: To install the package and skip its download, as a build server running only Playwright would, set `CYPRESS_INSTALL_BINARY` to ___ .
Coming from Playwright, a student runs `npx cypress run` without starting the shop first, and every test fails to load the page. What is the difference they missed?

choices.text: `baseUrl` has to name `127.0.0.1` instead of `localhost`
choices.why: Either name reaches the shop when it is running; here nothing is running.

choices.text: Cypress never starts the application; it must be running
choices.why: Right. Playwright's `webServer` starts the shop; Cypress has no such step, so it takes `npm start` in another terminal.

choices.text: `supportFile: false` turns off the part of Cypress that starts servers
choices.why: The support file holds shared commands; it has nothing to do with starting the application.

choices.text: The specs must live in `tests/`, beside Playwright's
choices.why: `specPattern` points Cypress at `cypress/e2e/`, and the specs were found; it was the page that failed.

prompt: A test says `const count = cy.get('[data-testid=basket-count]');` and then `count.text()`. What happens?

choices.text: `count` holds the element once the page has loaded
choices.why: Nothing has loaded yet: the call only queued a command, and returned the chain at once.

choices.text: A `TypeError`, before any command has run
choices.why: Right. `count` is a chain, which has no `text()`, and the test function is still writing the queue.

choices.text: It works, but only after waiting up to four seconds for the element
choices.why: The four seconds belong to commands in the queue; this line runs outside it, at once.

choices.text: It works if the line starts with `await`
choices.why: Commands are not promises, by Cypress's own documentation; `await` waits for nothing useful.

prompt: Put what happens in the first test of `shop.cy.js` in order, after `beforeEach`.
items: The test function runs and queues its commands
`cy.get` finds no items, and is tried again
The products arrive and the eight items are found
trap: Nothing in the queue runs while the test function is still running: queuing comes first, every time.

prompt: By the type definitions, how many milliseconds does a `should` keep retrying before it fails, if nobody changes `defaultCommandTimeout`?
Which of these is retried together with the `should` that follows it?

choices.text: `.click()`
choices.why: An action waits until the element can be clicked, then clicks once; repeating it would add a second banana.

choices.text: `cy.get('#products li')`
choices.why: Right. `cy.get` is a query, and queries are run again with the assertion until it passes.

choices.text: `cy.visit('/')`
choices.why: It loads the page once and waits for it to load; it is not a query.

choices.text: `cy.request('POST', '/api/reset')`
choices.why: Sending the reset twice would be a second request with an effect; it is sent once.

prompt: On a slow test server, the request behind Add to basket takes three seconds to answer. The test clicks, then checks the count with `should('have.text', '1')`. What happens?

choices.text: It fails, because the click is repeated and adds two
choices.why: Actions are not retried; only the query before the assertion is.

choices.text: It fails, because `should` checks once, right after the click
choices.why: `should` retries until it passes or the time runs out; that is what the queue is for.

choices.text: It passes: the check keeps trying, and three seconds is inside four
choices.why: Right. The count reads 0 for three seconds, then 1, well before the default four seconds run out.

choices.text: It passes only with a `cy.wait(3000)` before the check
choices.why: The retry already covers it, and a fixed sleep would be the habit section 05 replaces.

prompt: A test writes `cy.visit('/')`, then `cy.intercept('GET', '/api/products').as('products')`, then `cy.wait('@products')`. What goes wrong?

choices.text: Nothing: Cypress moves every route to the start of the test
choices.why: The queue keeps the order you wrote; the route exists only from its own step on.

choices.text: The products were asked for before the route existed
choices.why: Right. The page asks as soon as its script runs, during the visit; declare the route first.

choices.text: An alias has to be declared beforehand, in `cypress.config.js`
choices.why: `.as()` names the route in the test itself; the configuration knows nothing of it.

choices.text: `cy.wait` with an alias is meant for POST requests
choices.why: It waits for any method the route matches; the first test of `network.cy.js` waits for a GET.

prompt: Every test in a suite stubs `/api/products`. The shop then renames `price` to `cents` in that answer. What do the tests report?

choices.text: They fail, because Cypress compares each stub with the real answer
choices.why: A stub replaces the answer; the real server is never asked, so there is nothing to compare.

choices.text: They all keep passing
choices.why: Right. They test the page against a copy of yesterday's answer, which is why some tests must not stub.

choices.text: They fail on the next run, when the stub is refreshed
choices.why: The body is written in the test file and changes only when somebody edits it.

choices.text: Cypress prints a warning that the stub is stale
choices.why: Nothing in Cypress knows what the real server returns today.

prompt: You must check that the shop shows its list as busy while the products load, on every run. On a laptop that state lasts a few milliseconds. What works?

choices.text: Run the test many times over and keep whichever run happened to catch the moment
choices.why: A test that passes by luck is the flaky test lesson 14 is about; it will miss the moment on other days.

choices.text: `cy.wait(100)` after the visit, then check
choices.why: By then the list has usually loaded; a fixed sleep guesses at a moment it cannot see.

choices.text: Hold the answer back with `delay` in `cy.intercept`, then check `aria-busy`
choices.why: Right. The state lasts as long as the stub says, so the check meets it on every run.

choices.text: Check `aria-busy` before `cy.visit`
choices.why: Before the visit there is no page in the frame at all, busy or not.

prompt: In the `origins.mjs` capture, the page's own script was refused the `127.0.0.1` frame and Playwright read its title. Why the difference?

choices.text: Playwright switches off the same-origin policy for every page it launches
choices.why: The policy was on: the script inside the same browser was refused. Playwright simply was not asking as a script on the page.

choices.text: It asks through the browser's debugging protocol, from outside the page
choices.why: Right. The rule binds scripts on a page, and a driver outside the browser is not one.

choices.text: The frame had not finished loading when the script asked
choices.why: The script waited for each frame's `load`, and the same-origin frame answered at once.

choices.text: `127.0.0.1` is a different server from `localhost`
choices.why: Same server, same shop; the browser compares the text of the origin, and the texts differ.

prompt: A shop's sign-in happens on an identity provider at another domain, and the test must come back signed in. What does the Cypress test need?

choices.text: Nothing extra: its proxy turns every domain into one origin
choices.why: The proxy gives the runner the application's origin; a second domain is still a second origin.

choices.text: The sign-in steps inside `cy.origin`, values passed in through `args`
choices.why: Right. The function runs in the other origin, and as it is sent there as text, it reaches no variable around it.

choices.text: A second tab opened for the provider's page, then closed once signed in
choices.why: A Cypress test drives one tab; there is no second one to open.

choices.text: It cannot be done: a Cypress test stays on one domain for its whole life
choices.why: That was a belief worth holding once; `cy.origin` exists for exactly this case.

prompt: By its documentation, which of these can `cypress run --browser` not drive?

choices.text: Firefox
choices.why: Firefox is on the list, beside the Chrome family.

choices.text: Edge
choices.why: Edge is part of the Chrome family the documentation lists.

choices.text: Safari
choices.why: Right. There is a WebKit experiment behind a setting, and WebKit is not Safari.

choices.text: Electron
choices.why: Electron is the default; it ships inside the binary.

prompt: A checkout opens the payment provider in a new tab, and the client's customers mostly use Safari on iPhones. Which limits of Cypress does this meet? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A test drives one tab
choices.why: Right. The provider's tab is out of reach; the test can only check where the link points.

choices.text: Safari is not among the browsers it drives
choices.why: Right. The engine those customers use is the one Cypress offers only as an experiment, and Safari not at all.

choices.text: It cannot answer the payment request with a stub
choices.why: Stubbing a request is what `cy.intercept` does; this is not where the trouble is.

choices.text: It cannot run without a window
choices.why: `cypress run` is headless by default, in Electron.

prompt: Put a first Cypress session on your own computer in order.
items: `npm install`, which fetches the package and then the binary
`npx cypress verify`, to prove the binary starts
trap: Cypress does not start the shop, so it has to be running before the run, and nothing runs before the install.
